source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Deciduous elm, often on uplands or lowlands
morphology_documented.leaves: Relatively thick and stiff, blunt to subacute, harshly sandpapery above, usually doubly serrate (genus key)
morphology_documented.twigs: Some with corky wings, some without (key)

source_scope_note: Direct species-level details separated from genus/key information; absent historical treatments not filled by unsupported inference.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: 1999 flora emphasizes this is the only native Texas elm in its treatment that flowers in fall
Contrast with Ulmus alata (spring blooms, acuter, smoother leaves)
Historical flora discusses prairie invasion with fire suppression; not proof of Hays native status without county check
preservation: Additive record only; photos, credits, species records and published site unchanged
